draft.title: Changing trade links
card: Trade links between places are not fixed. They grow, shrink or shift to new partners over time.
After British settlement in 1788, Australia's trade was mostly with Britain. Wool, wheat and other farm goods went there by ship.
Today Australia trades mostly with countries in Asia, such as China, Japan and South Korea. Iron ore, coal, gas and education services are major exports.
Links change for many reasons. Britain joined a European trading group in the 1970s, Asian economies grew fast, and Asia is much closer to Australia.
draft.remember: Trade links shift over time, and Australia's main partners moved from Britain to Asia.

a.q: Which statement best describes how Australia's trade links have changed?
opts: Britain was the main partner once, and Asia is now
Asia was the main partner once, and Britain is now
Australia has always traded mostly with the same places
Australia stopped trading farm goods when it began mining
a.why: Australia's early trade was mostly with Britain, and today most trade is with Asian countries. The reverse order is wrong, and trade links are not fixed.
a.clue: Think about who Australia sold wool to in the past and who buys iron ore now.

b.q: Which is a reason why Australia's trade moved towards Asia?
opts: Asian economies grew fast and are close to Australia
Britain stopped having any need for goods from anywhere
Ships can no longer make the long trip to Britain
Australia stopped producing goods that people wanted
b.why: Fast-growing Asian economies wanted resources such as iron ore and coal, and Asia is nearby. Britain did not stop needing goods. The change came from new trading partners rising and Britain's own links shifting.
b.clue: Look for a reason about the new partners, not a claim that old trade ended completely.

a.best: Britain was the main partner once, and Asia is now

b.best: Asian economies grew fast and are close to Australia

problems.detail: The clue says to avoid 'a claim that old trade ended completely'. All three wrong options say something stopped ('no longer', 'stopped having any need', 'stopped producing'), so the clue rules them all out and gives the answer away.
